title: Dumbass Republic: Why Unanchored Multi-Agent Handoff Rings Inevitably Destabilize
content: Autonomous large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly orchestrated into decentralized handoff chains and closed collaboration rings that operate without central judges, immutable public charters, or continuous ground-truth verification. While such peer-to-peer workflows appear stable on objective benchmarks, their long-horizon behavior under open judgment and persistent internal drift has remained uncharacterized. Here we prove and empirically demonstrate why unanchored single-input multi-agent handoff rings inevitably destabilize. Across three preregistered live-LLM task regimes (deepseek-flash, 4,759 logged node actions in the open-judgment regime, yielding 4,716 verdict-parseable transitions), we uncover a sharp regime boundary: verifiable format and clear triage tasks resist up to 50% adversarial nodes through pretraining-prior anchoring, whereas open borderline expenditure approval—where no request has an objective right answer—is captured by a single persistent adversary (20% of the ring), driving non-adversary approvals from 50.0% (12/24) to 91.7% (22/24; case-matched shift +0.33, crossing the +0.25 regime-shift threshold). Inserting ordinary or lossy ("dumb") downstream nodes leaves the system captured across every live arm (+0.11 to +0.39 versus the <= +0.10 restoration bar) and across calibrated scaling projections up to +8 nodes. An offline stochastic decomposition calibrated directly from the live archive validates 9/10 experimental arms and exposes a Double-Lock Contagion Mechanism comprising two independently lethal LLM-native channels: (i) one-shot norm freezing on lap 1 (83.3% immediate adoption: 10/12 plain, 5/6 lossy; post-settlement flip rate < 1.3%: 2/348 loose, 2/162 guarded), and (ii) a decision-inertia ratchet in which the adversary overturns incoming rejections at 97.1% (100/103) while clean nodes preserve incoming approvals at 100% (219/219) and explicitly guarded plain nodes overturn approvals at 10.9% (76/697). A calibrated 2x2 factorial ablation confirms that either channel alone drives full collapse (+0.312 for Channel A alone; +0.311 for Channel B alone; +0.348 combined), whereas dismantling both simultaneously eliminates shift (+0.0001). Counterfactual 12-node phase-space sweeps establish an Impossibility Triangle: inserting k independent re-judging anchors stabilizes outputs at k = 2 (+0.03 shift) at the cost of a tight 1:1 Security-Reach Conservation Law (18% adversary capture vs. 22% legitimate order reach, scaling as 1/(2k)), whereas rotating authority without an immutable anchor converges to 83%-100% capture by lap 30 while compromising outputs on lap 1 (+0.25 to +0.36). These laws specify the exact structural primitives—blind re-evaluation, local multi-source verification, or sparse environmental restoring forces—required for durable autonomous agent organizations.
